ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.claim: The concluding discourse returns to the sūrah's opening theme: Qur'anic warnings are true, punishment signs can come, and prophetic histories already serve as signs for the stubborn Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.anchor: Coming up are the concluding verses of the sūrah and the discourse links to its introductory part which is the real theme.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r3.claim: The Qur'an is mentioned and signaled in earlier revealed books; alternatively, its meanings are present there, which Abū Ḥanīfa's permissibility of Persian prayer recitation is said to support.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r3.anchor: وإنه، أي القرآن لفي زبر الأولين: أي مذكور في الكتب المنزلة القديمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r4.claim: Another reading of the pronoun refers to Muhammad and says his mention and mission occur in prior scriptures; this better preserves a consistent referent for the nearby pronouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r4.anchor: وقيل: الضمير عائد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أي إن ذكره ورسالته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r5.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r5.claim: He reads zubur with a still bāʾ, though the underlying form has ḍamma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p189/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: لفي زبر، بسكون الباء، والأصل الضم

MAJAZ:v2p90/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p90/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p90/r7.claim: Zubur means the books of earlier peoples; its singular is zabūr.

SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r1.claim: The pronoun in wa-innahu refers to the Qurʾān.
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r1.anchor: أي: وإن القرآن. وقيل: وإن محمدا

SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r2.claim: Another view takes the pronoun to refer to Muḥammad.

SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r3.claim: The wording shifts person: continuation of the preceding direct address would have said wa-innaka, you are in the earlier scriptures.
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r3.anchor: وفيه التفات؛ إذ لو جرى على ما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r4.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:26:196/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads zubur with a vowelless bāʾ, a lightened form of the standard reading.

ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r1.claim: The earlier scriptures contain mention of Muhammad and the Qur'an.
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r1.anchor: تأويله والله أعلم أن ذكر محمد عليه السلام وذكر القرآن في زبر الأولين

ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r2.claim: Zubur means books; زبور and زبر form a singular-plural pair like رسول and رسل.
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r2.anchor: والزبر الكتب، زبور وزبر مثل قولك رسول ورسل

ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r3.claim: The claim is linked to the earlier description that they find him written in the Torah and Gospel.
ZAJJAJ:v4p100/r3.anchor: كما قال الله عز وجل: (يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم في التوراة والإنجيل).

ASAD-NOTES:26:196#n83/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:196#n83/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:196#n83/r1.claim: Zamakhshari and Baydawi (with an attribution by Zamakhshari to Abu Hanifah) take this to mean that the Qur'an's essential teachings match those of earlier prophets; Asad says this accords with the Qur'an's repeated doctrine.
ASAD-NOTES:26:196#n83/r1.anchor: is in full consonance with the oft-repeated Qur'anic doctrine that the basic teachings revealed to Muhammad

ASAD-NOTES:26:196#n83/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:196#n83/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:196#n83/r2.claim: A more popular alternative says that the Qur'an was mentioned or foretold in earlier scriptures, with references to 2:42 and 61:6.
ASAD-NOTES:26:196#n83/r2.anchor: Another, more popular interpretation is, "... this [Qur'an] has been mentioned

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the Quran's mention in earlier scriptures, with an omitted noun, as when someone is said to be in the governor's register.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r1.anchor: أي وان ذكر القرآن لفي الكتب المتقدمة على أن الضمير للقرآن والكلام على حذف مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the Quran's meaning is in earlier scriptures: they contain monotheism, accounts of God's essence and attributes, many admonitions, and stories, even if some Quranic material is absent.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : المراد وان معناه لفي الكتب المتقدمة وهو اعتبار الأغلب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa is famous for allowing Quran recitation in Persian and, by one report, Turkish, Indian, and other languages without restriction, citing this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r3.anchor: واشتهر عن الامام أبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه جوز قراءة القرءان بالفارسي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r4.claim: A second report limits permission to Persian, said to be the noblest language after Arabic, citing a report that Paradise's language is Arabic and Persian Duri.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r4.anchor: وفي رواية تخصيص الجواز بالفارسية لأنها أشرف اللغات بعد العربية لخبر لسان أهل الجنة العربي والفارسي الدري

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r5.claim: Another report permits Persian only for praise such as Surat al-Ikhlas, not for other Quranic content.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r5.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى أنها انما تجوز بالفارسية إذا كان ثناء كسورة الاخلاص أما إدا كان غيره فلا تجوز

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r6.speaker: الصاحبان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r6.claim: A further position allows Persian in prayer only for someone unable to recite Arabic and only for remembrance or glorification; it forbids it outside prayer, for an Arabic-capable worshipper, or for narrative and legal passages.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r6.anchor: هذا قول صاحبيه وكان رضي الله تعالى عنه قد ذهب إلى خلافه ثم رجع عنه اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r7.speaker: جمع من الثقات المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r7.claim: A number of reliable authorities authenticate that Abu Hanifa later recanted his unrestricted permission to recite in a non-Arabic language; Al-Alusi says the verse is weak evidence for that ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r7.anchor: وقد صحح رجوعه عن القول بجواز القراءة بغير العربية مطلقا جمع من الثقات المحققين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r8.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r8.claim: Al-Kashf argues that the Quran sent as a miracle cannot be a translation; if it is God's inner meaning, it is not recitable, while differing names for shared meanings show that the specific wording matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r8.anchor: فلا شك أن الترجمة ليست بقرآن وان كان هو المعنى القائم بصحابه فلاشك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r9.claim: Al-Alusi objects that 41:44 calls an imagined non-Arabic revelation 'Quran,' undermining the claim that only Arabic wording can bear that name.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r9.anchor: فان قوله تعالى ( ولو جعلناه قرآنا أعجميا ) يستلزم تسميته قرآنا أيضا لو كان أعجميا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r10.claim: The indefinite Quran has not departed from its lexical sense and can mean any recited text, while the definite 'the Quran' in religious usage means the Arabic text; this distinction explains the recitation command in 73:20. Reading 'from' partitive and taking a meaning as a part is untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r10.anchor: أما القرآن باللام فالمفهوم منه العربي في عرف الشرع فلخصوص العبارة مدخل في التسمية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r11.claim: A further opinion takes the pronoun to refer to the Messenger, but Al-Alusi says this is unclear.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r11.anchor: وقيل : ( إنه ) عائد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وليس بواضح

ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r12.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v19p125#3/r12.claim: Al-A'mash reads زبر with a quiescent bāʾ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r1.claim: Most exegetes take the pronoun to refer to the Qur’an’s mention in earlier scriptures.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r1.anchor: ذكر إنزال القرآن، قاله أكثر المفسرين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r2.claim: Muqatil instead takes the pronoun to refer to Muhammad and his description in earlier scriptures.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p129/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ذكر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ونعته

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r3.claim: What is in the earlier books is either the Qur'an's mention or its meaning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:195-197/r3.anchor: وإن ذكره أو معناه لفي الكتب المتقدمة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s foundations, many narratives, and principal teachings are found in earlier scriptures, established books that their communities recognize as divinely sent.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r7.anchor: { وإنه } اي هذا القرآن أصوله وكثير من قصصه وأمهات فروعه { لفي زبر } أي كتب { الأولين * } المضبوطة الظاهرة في كونها أتت من السماء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r8.claim: Because Muhammad had no contact with those earlier communities to learn their scriptures, this correspondence is decisive evidence that God revealed the Qur’an.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p391/r8.anchor: من غير أن يخالط هذا الذي جاء به أحدا منهم أو من غيرهم في علم ما , وكان ذلك دليلا قاطعا على أنه ما أتاه به إلا الله تعالى .

DURR-FULL:v6p321/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r4.claim: Ibn Salām recounts Quraysh’s encounter with Jews reading Torah, the Jews’ disavowal of people who slandered it for worldly gain, and the revelation that the Prophet, his description, and his mission were in earlier scriptures.
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سلام قال: كان نفر من قريش من أهل مكة قدموا على قوم من يهود من بني قريظة

DURR-FULL:v6p321/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase refers to the books God revealed to earlier peoples.
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد {وإنه لفي زبر الأولين} يقول: في الكتب التي أنزلها على الأولين

DURR-FULL:v6p321/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r6.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as the books of earlier peoples.
DURR-FULL:v6p321/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وإنه لفي زبر الأولين} قال: كتب الأولين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819/r1.claim: Qatāda says the Qurʾān is in the books of earlier peoples; the same gloss is reported from al-Suddī.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وانه لفي زبر الاولين اي : في كتب الاولين . وروي ، عن السدي مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819/r2.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says it means the scriptures God sent down to earlier peoples.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2819/r2.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : لفي زبر الاولين قال : يقول التي انزلها على الاولين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r1.claim: The earlier writings are the books of earlier prophets, including the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and other scriptures known collectively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r1.anchor: وقوله : { في زبر الأولين } أي كتب الرسل السالفين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r2.claim: The pronoun cannot mean the Qur’an’s revealed wording, since its sūras and verses are not written verbatim in earlier scriptures; it refers instead to its name, distinctive description, or meanings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r2.anchor: إذ ليست سور القرآن وآياته مسطورة في زبر الأولين بلفظها كله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r3.claim: On the name-and-description reading, earlier books foretold Muhammad and a messenger who would bring a book, as in the Qur’an’s report that the unlettered Prophet is written in the Torah and Gospel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r3.anchor: فالمعنى أن ذكر القرآن وارد في كتب الأولين ، أي جاءت بشارات بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r4.claim: In Deuteronomy 18 Moses promises a prophet like himself from his brethren; Ibn ʿĀshūr identifies Israel’s brethren as Arabs, citing Ishmael’s descendants living opposite their brethren, and sees no other post-Mosaic prophet bringing comparable law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r4.anchor: ففي سفر التثنية من كتب موسى عليه السلام في الإصحاح الثامن عشر قول موسى : ( قال لي الرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r5.claim: The Deuteronomy promise that God will put His words in the prophet’s mouth refers to the Qur’an revealed to Muhammad, which he recites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r5.anchor: وكلام الله المجعول في فمه هو القرآن الموحى به إليه وهو يتلوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r6.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r6.claim: As quoted in Matthew 24, Jesus warns of many false prophets and says the enduring message will be preached throughout the inhabited world as testimony to all nations before the end.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r6.anchor: وفي إنجيل متى الإصحاح الرابع والعشرين قال عيسى عليه السلام : ( ويقوم أنبياء كذبة كثيرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reads that universal proclamation as the revelation and Qur’an addressed to all peoples, linking it to the Qur’an’s statements about guiding humanity and setting out every kind of example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p191/r7.anchor: فالبشارة هي الوحي وهو القرآن وهو الكتاب الذي دعا جميع الأمم

BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to mention of the Qur'an, not the Qur'an itself.
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r1.anchor: أي : وإن ذكر القرآن لا عينه

BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r2.claim: Zubur is the plural of zabūr, meaning books; the Qur'an's mention and the final Prophet's coming were in earlier scriptures.
BURSEVI:v6p223#2/r2.anchor: واحدها زبور بمعنى الكتاب مثل رسل ورسول ، أي لفي الكتب المتقدمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r11.claim: The Qur'an was mentioned and pointed to in the earlier revealed books.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r11.anchor: أي في كتبهم يريد القرآن أنه مذكور في الكتب المنزلة القديمة منبه عليه مشار إليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r12.speaker: الجمهور والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p242#2/r12.claim: Most pronounce the b of زبر with damma; al-Aʿmash reads it with sukūn.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r1.speaker: الأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads zubur with a quiescent bāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r1.anchor: وقرأ الاعمش زبر بتسكين الباء وفي هاء الكناية قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r2.claim: Most commentators say the pronoun refers to the Quran, meaning that its mention and account occur in the earlier scriptures.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنها ترجع إلى القرآن والمعنى وإن ذكر القرآن وخبره هذا قول الأكثرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r3.claim: Muqatil says the pronoun refers to the Messenger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p144#3/r3.anchor: والثاني أنها تعود إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاله مقاتل

JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r9.claim: Zubur are books; zabūr is singular, and the root means collecting and writing.
JISHUMI:v7p5386#2/r9.anchor: الزبر: الكتب، واحدها: زبور، زبرت الكتاب أزبره زبرا: كتبته، وأصل الباب الجمع.

JISHUMI:v7p5390/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5390/r7.speaker: بعض أصحاب أبي حنيفة
JISHUMI:v7p5390/r7.claim: Some followers of Abū Ḥanīfa infer that the Qurʾān remains Qurʾān in a non-Arabic language.
JISHUMI:v7p5390/r7.anchor: واستدل بعض أصحاب أبي حنيفة بقوله: (وإنه لفي زبر الأولين) أن القرآن قرآن وإن كان بغير لغة العرب،

JISHUMI:v7p5390/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5390/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5390/r8.claim: He rejects this: earlier scriptures mentioned its content; Qurʾān comprises wording and meaning.
JISHUMI:v7p5390/r8.anchor: وهذا لا يصح؛ لأن معناه ما ذكر فيه على ما بينا؛ لأن - القرآن ما كان بلفظه ومعناه.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r4.claim: Each repeated story is like a self-contained revelation and merits the same opening and conclusion because each carries its own lesson.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r4.anchor: كل قصة منها كتنزيل برأسه ، وفيها من الاعتبار مثل ما في غيرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r5.claim: Repetition fixes meanings in the soul and memory: repeated review strengthens understanding and makes knowledge harder to forget.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r5.anchor: ولأن في التكرير تقريرا للمعاني في الأنفس ، وتثبيتا لها في الصدور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r6.claim: The stories are repeated because listeners are deaf to truth and hearts closed to reflection; reiteration may open ears and minds and polish understanding dulled by neglect.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p338#4/r6.anchor: ولأن هذه القصص طرقت بها آذان وقر عن الإنصات للحق ، وقلوب غلف عن تدبره

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r1.claim: The earlier scriptures here include the Torah, Gospel, and other revealed books.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r1.anchor: يعني كتب الأولين من التوراة والإنجيل وغيرها من الكتب

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the Qur’an is mentioned in the earlier scriptures.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r2.anchor: أحدها : أن المراد به ذكر القرآن في زبر الأولين , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Muhammad’s mission is recorded in the earlier scriptures.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : بعث محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في زبر الأولين , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the earlier scriptures mention Muhammad’s religion and describe his community.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p187#2/r4.anchor: الثالث : ذكر دينك وصفة أمتك في زبر الأولين , قاله الضحاك

MUQATIL:26:190-200/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:190-200/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:190-200/r8.claim: The earlier scriptures contain accounts of Muhammad and descriptions of him.
MUQATIL:26:190-200/r8.anchor: وإنه لفي زبر الأولين } [آية: 196] يقول: أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ونعته فى كتب الأولين.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p198/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the Quran, whose mention is recorded in the heavenly scriptures.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198/r1.anchor: يعنى ذكره مثبت فى سائر الكتب السماوية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p198/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198/r2.claim: An alternative says the Quran's meanings are in earlier scriptures; this is used to argue a Persian translation counts as Quran for prayer recitation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p198/r2.anchor: وقيل إن معانيه فيها دليل أ القرآن قرآن إذا ترجم بغير العربية فيكون دليلا على جواز قراءة القرآن بالفارسية فى الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r7.claim: One reading is that mention of the Qurʾān's descent appears in the books of earlier prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r7.anchor: أي وإن ذكر نزوله لفي كتب الأولين يعني الأنبياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r8.claim: Another reading is that Muḥammad himself is mentioned in earlier books, including the Torah and Gospel.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r8.anchor: وقيل: أي إن ذكر محمد عليه السلام في كتب الأولين. كما قال تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r9.claim: Zubur means books; its singular zabūr forms a plural like rasūl and rusul.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:192-196/r9.anchor: والزبر الكتب الواحد زبور كرسول ورسل وقد تقدم.

RAZI-FULL:v24p142#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p142#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p142#2/r2.claim: The earlier scriptures strengthen the proof: the seven prophetic narratives match their accounts without discrepancy, although Muhammad had not studied or prepared for them.
RAZI-FULL:v24p142#2/r2.anchor: لما ذكر هذه القصص السبع على ما هي موجودة في زبر الأولين من غير تفاوت أصلا

RAZI-FULL:v24p145/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p145/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p145/r1.claim: The pronoun may refer to the preceding reports, the Quran’s description, Muhammad’s description, or the warnings already discussed.
RAZI-FULL:v24p145/r1.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد صفة القرآن

STUDYQURAN:26:196/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:196/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:26:196/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:196/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:26:196/r2.claim: Ṭ says the Quran is mentioned or described in scriptures revealed to earlier prophets.
STUDYQURAN:26:196/r2.anchor: the Quran is mentioned or described in some of the previous scriptures revealed to other prophets (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:26:196/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:196/r3.speaker: Th
STUDYQURAN:26:196/r3.claim: Th says the Prophet himself is mentioned in earlier scriptures.
STUDYQURAN:26:196/r3.anchor: the Prophet himself is so mentioned (Th)

TABATABAI:26:194-197/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r6.claim: The pronoun refers to the Qur’an or its descent upon Muhammad: news of the Qur’an or its descent appears in the books of earlier prophets.
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r6.anchor: الضمير للقرآن أو نزوله على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والزبر جمع زبور وهو الكتاب

TABATABAI:26:194-197/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r7.claim: Another view takes the pronoun to mean that Qur’anic universal truths already appear in earlier prophets’ books; the author objects that polytheists did not accept those books and this fails to fit the next verse.
TABATABAI:26:194-197/r7.anchor: وقيل الضمير لما في القرآن من المعارف الكلية أي إن المعارف القرآنية موجودة مذكورة في كتب الأنبياء الماضين

TABRISI:26:192-196/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:192-196/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:192-196/r16.claim: The Quran and news of Muhammad appear in earlier scriptures as glad tidings; this does not mean God revealed the Quran to anyone besides Muhammad. Zubur is plural of zabūr.
TABRISI:26:192-196/r16.anchor: أي في كتب الأولين على وجه البشارة به وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لا بمعنى أن الله أنزله على غير محمد

TABRISI:26:192-196/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:192-196/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:192-196/r17.claim: Another view says earlier prophets taught the same call to monotheism, justice, and resurrection, and related accounts of nations.
TABRISI:26:192-196/r17.anchor: وقيل. معناه أنه أنزل على سائر الأنبياء من الدعاء إلى التوحيد والعدل

THALABI:v7p179/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p179/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v7p179/r4.claim: Most commentators take the pronoun to mean the Quran's mention and account in the books of earlier peoples.
THALABI:v7p179/r4.anchor: وإنه يعني ذكر القرآن وخبره عن أكثر المفسرين

THALABI:v7p179/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p179/r5.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v7p179/r5.claim: Muqatil says the reference is to the mention and description of Muhammad in earlier scriptures.
THALABI:v7p179/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني ذكر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ونعته لفي زبر كتب الأولين

THALABI:v7p179/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p179/r6.speaker: الأعمش
THALABI:v7p179/r6.claim: Al-A'mash reads zubur with a quiescent ba; other readers use the vowelled form.
THALABI:v7p179/r6.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش زبر بجزم الباء، وغيره بالرفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r1.claim: The Quran and its account are recorded in earlier scriptures; God told them of its revelation to the Prophet sent at the end of time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r1.anchor: وإن ذكر القرآن وخبره لفي كتب الأولين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r2.claim: The matter, mention, and description of Muhammad are in the earlier scriptures.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: وإن أمر محمد، وذكره، ونعته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r3.claim: Zubur means books; zabūr and zubur form a singular and plural pattern like rasūl and rusul.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p124#2/r3.anchor: والزبر: الكتب، زبور وزبر، مثل: رسول ورسل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:196-197/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:196-197/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:196-197/r1.claim: The mention of Muhammad is found in the books of earlier peoples.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:196-197/r1.anchor: ذكر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { لفي زبر الأولين } لفي كتب الأولين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r6.claim: Qatadah says the Qur'an is found in the earlier books, the Torah and Gospel.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r6.anchor: قال قتادة: أي: وإن القرآن لفي كتب الأولين، التوراة والإنجيل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r7.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says the earlier books contain the description of Muhammad and his community.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p523/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: {وإنه لفي زبر الأولين} [الشعراء: 196] يقول: نعت محمد وأمته في زبر الأولين

ELMALILI:26:192-209/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r8.claim: The Quran's mention also occurs in the books of earlier peoples.
ELMALILI:26:192-209/r8.anchor: evvelkilerin kitaplarında da vardır yani evvelki kitaplarda da bu Kur’ân’ın zikri geçmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r1.claim: The meaning and essential message revealed to Muhammad had already appeared, in its basic outlines, in earlier scriptures such as the Psalms, Torah, and Gospel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r1.anchor: mesajın mânası ve özü, temel çizgileri itibariyle önceki peygamberlere gelmiş olan Zebûr, Tevrat, İncil vb. kitaplarda da vardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r2.speaker: Şevkânî, İbn Âşûr, Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r2.claim: A reported interpretation is that earlier prophets' books foretold the Qur'an's coming; the author allows this meaning alongside the prior-message interpretation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r2.anchor: Bir görüşe göre de Kur’an’ın indirileceği önceki, peygamberlerin kitaplarında haber verilmişti (Şevkânî, IV, 113; İbn Âşûr, XIX, 191-192; Esed, II, 758)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r3.claim: The wording may intend both that the Qur'an's essential message was present in earlier scriptures and that its coming was foretold.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:196/r3.anchor: Âyette bu anlamların her ikisi de kastedilmiş olabilir

ITQAN:v4p317/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p317/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p317/r1.claim: The Quran’s summary proof of inimitability is that Arabs could not match it despite its Arabic language; detailed proof comes from reflecting on its composition and recognizing its source as all-knowing.
ITQAN:v4p317/r1.anchor: فعلى إعجازه دليل إجمالي وهو أن العرب عجزت عنه وهو بلسانها فغيرها أحرى ودليل تفصيلي مقدمته التفكر في خواص تركيبه

ITQAN:v4p317/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p317/r2.speaker: الأصبهاني
ITQAN:v4p317/r2.claim: Al-Isfahani distinguishes intrinsic inimitability from God’s diverting people from competition; the Quran’s distinctive inimitability lies in its particular composition, not its Arabic words or meanings also found in earlier scriptures.
ITQAN:v4p317/r2.anchor: وقال الأصبهاني في تفسيره اعلم أن إعجاز القرآن ذكر من وجهين أحدهما إعجاز يتعلق بنفسه والثاني بصرف الناس عن معارضته

ITQAN:v4p317/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p317/r3.speaker: الأصبهاني
ITQAN:v4p317/r3.claim: Al-Isfahani says the Quran’s composition is its form, while words and meanings are its elements; changes of form, like making gold into a ring, earring, or bracelet, change a thing’s name and status.
ITQAN:v4p317/r3.anchor: فإذن النظم المخصوص صورة القرآن واللفظ والمعنى عنصره وبإختلاف الصور يختلف حكم الشيء واسمه لا بعنصره

ITQAN:v4p317/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p317/r4.speaker: الأصبهاني
ITQAN:v4p317/r4.claim: Al-Isfahani begins describing five levels of composition: joining letters into words, then arranging words into meaningful sentences used in ordinary speech.
ITQAN:v4p317/r4.anchor: مراتب تأليف الكلام خمس الأولى ضم الحروف المبسوطة بعضها إلى بعض لتحصل الكلمات الثلاث الإسم والفعل والحروف والثانية تأليف هذه الكلمات بعضها إلى بعض

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r1.claim: Zubūr is the plural of zabūr, a book; al-Zajjaj says a zabūr is any book containing wisdom. Zabartu al-kitāb means ‘I wrote the book.’
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r1.anchor: الزبر : جمع زبور . والزبور : الكتاب . وقال الزجاج : الزبور كل كتاب ذو حكمة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p337/r4.claim: The second sense is books or scriptures, including the statement that the Qurʾan is found in the books of the ancients.

DAMGHANI:v1p215/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p215/r4.claim: Zubur can mean the scriptures of earlier peoples, as in the verse about what was written in the Zabūr.
DAMGHANI:v1p215/r4.anchor: الثاني : الزبر الكتب قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p447/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p447/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p447/r3.claim: Earlier scriptures predicted the Qur’an, and Israelite scholars know these prophecies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p447/r3.anchor: Previous scriptures have predicted it and the scholars of the Israelites are aware of these prophesies.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r11.claim: Proponents of the arrangement theory argue that Quranic words are ordinary Arabic and many meanings occur in earlier books, while unseen knowledge is miraculous regardless of language or form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r11.anchor: ولا بمعانيه فإن كثيرا منها موجود في الكتب المتقدمة
